responseText:
Short, practical rules of thumb:

- Obvious delete: spam, marketing you never open, and things you can’t act on or don’t need later (coupons that expired, one-time promo codes). If you never open a sender’s messages after a month, delete and unsubscribe.

- Delete after use: single-use notifications (password resets, delivery confirmations) once you’ve acted on them and there’s no need for a record.

- Tuck (archive/label): receipts, invoices, warranty info, contracts, tax or legal records, or anything you might need to search for later. Keep these for the required retention period.

- Tuck: ongoing threads or projects you may revisit — archive and add a project label so they’re findable without cluttering the inbox.

- Delete: duplicate or low-value newsletters you don’t read. If you might want similar content later, unsubscribe and delete now; if you want to keep occasional issues, tuck.

- Tuck (sentimental): personal notes you want to keep but don’t need in your inbox — put them in a “Memories” label.

- When unsure: ask “Will I need this within 90 days or is it legally/financially important?” If no → delete. If yes → tuck.

Quick note on terms: archiving/tucking keeps messages searchable and recoverable; deleting removes them (may be permanent depending on your provider). I won’t delete or archive anything for you unless you ask and give explicit confirmation about which messages.
